chunks: And from him, from Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Hashim al-Bajali, from Abi Khadijah, who said:

I saw Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) when he was slaughtering a camel with its left leg tied, then he stood on the side of its right leg and said, 'In the name of Allah, and Allah is the Greatest. O Allah, this is from You and for You. O Allah, accept it from me.' Then he stabbed its throat (labyrinth), then he removed the knife with his hand. When its sides had settled, he cut the place of slaughter with his hand. And whoever wishes to slaughter or perform nadhr, let him supplicate at the time of slaughter with what has been narrated:

key_terms.يَنْحَرُ: to slaughter (specifically by cutting the throat)

ai.seo_question: What is the correct supplication and physical procedure for slaughtering an animal according to Imam al-Sadiq (AS)?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* provides a detailed practical demonstration of the Prophet Muhammad’s method of slaughtering a camel, emphasizing the specific standing position and the recitation of the formula 'From You and for You, O Allah, accept it from me.' It serves as a primary source for the recommended supplication (du'a) during slaughter, linking the physical act of *dhabh* with spiritual intention, and is frequently cited by Shia jurists to validate the permissibility and etiquette of animal sacrifice.
